The one input a panel setting picks fills the BENCH rpm register and feeds the motor stall action. The panel already enables and places a rotation input by setting ('Optical tacho' SET_OPTICAL_EN, 'Tacho pin' SET_OPTICAL_PIN, -1 to 48), and the BENCH page carries one rpm register (LINK_BN_RPM = 3) with one valid bit (LINK_BN_RPM_OK, bit 2). Hardware consequence: every rotation input keeps its own front end and GPIO on the measurement coprocessor (Pins.md), none is multiplexed, so any one can be picked. Derived from the tree; no owner figure and no external source

65,535 rpm, the highest speed the BENCH rpm register carries (to_u16 saturates at 65,535). The owner's V225 answer uses the same figure as the highest rpm ('2.54 us of delay variation at 65,535 rpm'). Consequences: a once-per-revolution input and the vibration fundamental reach 1,092.25 Hz; the phase-wire clip, which reads the electrical frequency (V293), reaches 22,937 Hz at 21 pole pairs (MOTOR_POLES even, 2 to 42). For comparison, a commercial stand's optical probe reads 'up to 30,000 RPM' (Flight Stand 50 datasheet) and its electrical probe 0 to 190k eRPM (Series 1585 datasheet)

1.244 us of delay variation at 1,092 Hz (65,535 rpm) for the optical index: the sensor, its front end and the index comparator together. Found from V225 and V290: 1 degree of the 915.5 us period at 65,535 rpm is 2.543 us for the whole chain (V225); R10's own share is 52 ns, its 30 ps aperture jitter and the chip-select trigger jitter inside (V290, V291); the rest is split equally between the accelerometer and the optical index, (2.543 - 0.052) / 2 = 1.246 us, which V290 writes as 1.244 us. The split leaves no separate share for the index comparator, so its delay counts inside the 1.244 us. At 10,000 rpm the same split gives (16.67 - 0.342) / 2 = 8.16 us

report.value: Two PIO state machines in PIO0 of the measurement coprocessor (encoder A, B and I on GPIO 20, 21, 22), one per channel, run one copy of quad_edge.pio (19 instruction words); no external decoder, no DMA channel, no PWM slice for A and B. Each edge takes at most 6 clk_sys cycles (40 ns at 150 MHz) against 100 ns between one channel's edges at 5 MHz (80 ns at 40/60 duty), so 2 state machines decode 20 Mcounts/s; 1 MHz single-ended is 4 Mcounts/s. A cycle model with the 2-flipflop input synchroniser decodes 40,000 counts at 5 MHz without error at A-to-B spacing 30 and 70 ns, duty 40 to 60 %, 3 ns jitter and 200 reversals, and 1 MHz with 50 reversals; it decodes down to 14 ns of A-to-B spacing and fails at 13 ns. The receiver's opposite-edge delay difference across two channels of one AM26LV32EIDR is at most 26 - 8 = 18 ns (tPLH and tPHL 8 to 26 ns; the 9 ns tsk(pp) is a device-to-device figure and does not apply), which leaves 32 ns; the model decodes 32 ns at 40, 50 and 60 % duty with 3 ns jitter and 100 reversals. The counts sit in the RX FIFO in put mode (FJOIN_RX_PUT), read at any time; net = Y(A) - X(A) + X(B) - Y(B) modulo 2^32; a read while the shaft turns can mix counts a few edges apart, and the error does not accumulate. The index I is captured on the same chip's clock, by a GPIO edge interrupt on the 1 us system timer or by PIO. pico-examples' one-state-machine quadrature_encoder reads only sysclk / 10 = 15 Msteps/s. No quadrature decoder from an allowlisted maker is in the jlcparts copy. Derived from the datasheet's instruction timing and the model; not run on hardware; the program is not in the tree

1 degree at 65,535 rpm is 2.543 us for the whole chain (V225). R10: 52 ns, its 30 ps aperture jitter and the chip-select trigger jitter inside (V290, V291). Accelerometer: 1.244 us. Optical index: 1.244 us, its sensor, front end and index comparator together, since the split leaves the comparator no share of its own (V292 found). At 10,000 rpm: 16.67 us, R10 342 ns, 8.16 us each. The accelerometer's derived 1.000 us (ADXL316WBCSZ, 100 pF) leaves 0.244 us of its share unused

No optical sensor found meets the 1.244 us of V292, so the optical index has no survivor again. Integrated reflective sensors of allowed makers with stock use phototransistors and state 10 to 70 us: VCNT2030 10 / 15 us typical, VCNT2020 10 us typical and 70 us maximum, QRE1113 20 / 20 us, QRD1114 10 / 50 us, RPR-220 10 us; TCRT5000, TCRT5000L, CNY70 and TCRT1000 state no time. TCND5000 (Vishay, PIN photodiode, 2 to 25 mm range, JLCPCB C145489 308) states only the photodiode's 1.8 pF at VR 5 V and no detector time; Sensing.md:118 lists it among the sensors that state 10 to 70 us, which its datasheet does not. Discrete PIN photodiodes state times inside the share at their test conditions (BPV10NF tr 80 ns, tf 60 ns typical at VR 10 V, RL 50 Ohm; BPW34 100 ns at VR 10 V, RL 1 kOhm), but they state no working distance and need an emitter and an amplifier; a 3.3 V supply biases them below the 10 V of those conditions. Under V290's split a VCNT2030-class sensor (10 or 15 us typical, plus TLV3201's 55 ns) holds its share up to 8,108 rpm on the rising edge and 5,415 rpm on the falling edge; with the accelerometer's derived 1.000 us in place of its share, the whole-chain 1 degree holds up to 14,767 and 10,168 rpm. Owner decision: (a) TCND5000 with its detector time measured on the bench, as the datasheet states none; (b) a discrete emitter, PIN photodiode and amplifier on the probe board, its working distance measured on the bench; (c) the optical index qualified at a lower highest rpm than 65,535 with a phototransistor sensor; (d) a changed split of V225

The chosen 100 pF on XOUT is the whole node. The 2 m lead's capacitance is not known (cable not chosen, stage 2), so a buffer on the sensor board between XOUT and the lead keeps the node at 100 pF; no function selects that buffer. With RFILT 27 to 37 kOhm, 124 pF in all keeps the 1.244 us share at 1,092 Hz. Both datasheets recommend a minimum CX of 0.0047 uF; 100 pF is 47 times below it, and the output's behaviour there is not stated. With 0.0047 uF the variation is 22.9 us (8.99 degrees), and 1 degree then holds only up to 3,557 rpm. The owner decides whether the node below the recommendation is accepted and whether R11 selects the buffer
